name: UE4SS C++ mod
summary: A native UE4SS mod: a dll built against the UE4SS source. For what Lua is too slow or too limited to do.
description: The workspace the UE4SS docs describe: RE-UE4SS as a git submodule next to your mod's folder, built together, giving dlls\main.dll in the mod folder. Needs Visual Studio, git, Rust and a GitHub account linked to Epic Games. The first build compiles UE4SS itself and takes a while.

options.label: Mod name
options.patternHelp: start with a letter; letters, digits, spaces, - and _ only
options.help: The mod folder, the build target and the C++ class are this name without spaces.

options.label: Author
options.patternHelp: start with a letter; letters, digits, spaces, - and _ only

options.label: Description
options.help: Shown in the UE4SS mod list.

options.label: Game folder
options.help: The game's top folder. install.bat finds the UE4SS Mods folder under it. Leave empty to copy the dll by hand.

options.label: UE4SS version in the game
options.help: A C++ mod only loads in the UE4SS version it was built against. The first lines of UE4SS.log say which one the game has.

options.label: RE-UE4SS tag, branch or commit
options.patternHelp: a git tag, branch or commit id
options.help: Leave empty for the tag that goes with the version above (v3.0.1, experimental-latest, experimental2).

options.label: CMake generator
options.patternHelp: a CMake generator name, like Visual Studio 17 2022
options.help: The Visual Studio you have installed, as CMake names it (cmake --help lists them).

options.label: Enable with enabled.txt
options.help: On: install.bat puts an enabled.txt in the mod folder. Off: it adds the mod to mods.txt, which also fixes its load order.

next: Link your GitHub account to your Epic Games account and add an SSH key to GitHub: UE4SS pulls Unreal's headers from a private repo.
Run setup.bat once: it makes the folder a git repo and adds RE-UE4SS as a submodule at the right version.
Run build.bat. The first build compiles UE4SS too.
Run install.bat: it copies the dll to Mods\<mod>\dlls\main.dll in the game.
Start the game and look for the mod's "loaded" line in UE4SS.log.
Your code is in the mod's dllmain.cpp.
